posts.title: We can now build considerably more, but should we?
posts.description: Take the application on your computer that you’re most familiar with. Now imagine its creators opening up the product roadmap to 100 randomly selected users. They would build every feature request, idea, and redesign these people would come up with for half a year. Do you think you would still use that tool in two years time?

posts.title: You don't hire juniors to do menial chores
posts.description: There is this line of thought that has been bugging me for a while now: “With the coming of LLMs we don’t need juniors anymore”. The idea is that all the boring work (boilerplate, etc.) can be handled by LLMs, and we can now just focus on the real work. As you’ve probably heard a million times by now, the counterargument to not hiring juniors is the question of succession. Who will be your future

posts.title: Movement is not progress
posts.description: The market is in a weird place right now, a lot of companies are making record profits, but at the same time every other company seems to think bankruptcy is around the corner. Both of these camps seem to use the same general strategy: cut costs and maximize profits. What mainly comes down to: getting more money.
